notes:
WHERE IT IS: The list begins on page 54 (n69.jpg) under the heading "LIST OF STATIONS." and continues on page 55 (n70.jpg), ending just before "Diary from the Stations." I could see both the start and the end on those two images, so I didn't open n67 (p. 52, running text), n68 or n71. There are 35 stations: nos. 81–114 plus 109B. That matches the lead-in, "Schedules, etc., were sent to thirty-five stations". The 15 starred rows match "we have received returns from fifteen stations".

COLUMNS: The column heads are "Returns in 8 years, including 1887." | "In 1887." | "List of Stations." | "Values." | "Feet." The "In 1887" column holds only the * mark, so marks="*" means a return in this report's season. The report says it covers schedules from August 1886 to February 1887, which is why "1887" appears in the column heads of the 1886 report. The returns count is the bare first figure; I put it in `other` as "Returns in 8 years: N". Dot leaders are shortened to "........" in `printed`.

NO KEEPERS: No names are printed in the list. A note set sideways down the right margin of both pages reads: "The names of the Reporters are given under 'Diary from the Stations.'" So every `keepers` field is []. To build the keeper roll you'll need the Diary section that starts on p. 55. For example: Butt of Lewis — Robert Agnew, replacing Mr Edgar, now at Lochindaul; Mr Joseph Agnew is now at Monach Isles. No light characters or L.H./L.V. types are printed; every station is a lighthouse by implication.

SUB-HEADINGS: There are only two: "SUTHERLAND." (nos. 81–82) and "OUTER HEBRIDES." (nos. 83 onward). Page 55 is headed "OUTER HEBRIDES—continued." and has no further sub-heading. So Skye, Mull, Islay, the Clyde, Ayrshire and Galloway (91–114) are all printed under "Outer Hebrides", which is geographically wrong. I've kept "Outer Hebrides" as `coast`, as printed. Both headings are in small capitals.

ODD ROWS:
- 84 Stornoway: "(2 Lights)" follows the name. It has two values stacked in a brace ({II. / I.}) and one height, 56, joined to both values by a closing brace. Because the braces belong to the value/feet columns, I described them in `other` and didn't treat them as a station mark.
- 86 Monach Islands: two values stacked in a brace (I. / II.) and two heights (150 / 62).
- 92 Ardnamurchan: no comma after the name and no height.
- 105 Sanda and 109B Ailsa Craig: no value and no height.
- 109B: the "B" is a small capital ("109B"). "1885" is printed after the name, probably the year the light was added or first lit; I put it in `other`.
- 93: the name runs over two lines ("Skerryvore and Hynish Signal / Tower, Tiree,"); I joined them into one.
- 100: M‘Arthur’s has a turned comma (‘) after M; I kept it.

VALUES SCALE: The other reader described the values as I–V, but "VI." is printed for 87 Ushenish, 98 Fladda and 104 Mull of Cantyre. So the scale runs at least to VI.

SPELLINGS (copied as printed, not corrected; modern or usual forms in brackets): Rhu Stoir (Rubh' Stoer/Stoer Head); Island Ghlais (Eilean Glas, Scalpay); Ushenish; Dhuheartach (Dubh Artach); Rhuvaal (Rubh' a' Mhàil); Skervuile; Lochindaul (Loch Indaal); Mull of Cantyre (Kintyre); Devaar (Davaar). The list says "Monach Islands" but the Diary says "Monach Isles".

READING: Everything was legible on the scans and no row has an unsure reading. The star before 89 is printed slightly differently from the others but is clearly an asterisk. The OCR garbled several figures (for example 85's "180958", 104's returns, and 102's returns as "eF"); I read all of them from the images.
